clue.text: Recovered ground in team again?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: given a new covering, as a worn tyre is given a fresh tread
second meaning: back on the field because picked for the national side once more

explanation.surface: A side has won back lost territory and is pondering whether to field the same players.
explanation.walkthrough: A player picked for England is said to win a cap, so one restored to the side is capped again; a tyre given a new tread is also recapped.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both re-treaded or re-covered and selected once more for a representative sporting side.

clue.text: Beak the staff used to put in charge

definitions.note: the definition is the thing used to put in the charge, a noun

parts.note: a ram is the projecting beak on the prow of an old warship
a staff is a rod or stick

explanation.surface: A magistrate, the beak in British slang, names the officials who will run things.
explanation.walkthrough: Beak and charge both pretend to be about courts and command; the charge is really the powder rammed down a gun barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A muzzle-loading gun was loaded by pushing powder and shot down the barrel with this rod.

clue.text: Loses race, having altered type of course

indicators.note: something altered has been changed, so the letters before it are put into a new order

parts.note: the letters of both words, taken together

explanation.surface: A runner who loses has changed the kind of track they run on.
explanation.walkthrough: Race and course pull towards athletics; the course is a dish at a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew cooked slowly in the oven is served as the main dish at a meal.

clue.text: Part of London University included in demand

indicators.note: something included is taken inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Poplar is a district of East London
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A popular college of the University of London attracts plenty of applicants.
explanation.walkthrough: Part of London University reads as one college, but it splits: Part of London, then University.
explanation.definitionFit: Something widely liked and sought after by many people is said to be much wanted.

clue.text: Forward almost losing head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is dropped here

parts.note: a synonym for almost

explanation.surface: A striker who has almost lost their head in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Forward looks like a football player; it is the adjective meaning advanced or precocious.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward spring or a forward child is one that comes on ahead of the usual time.

clue.text: Reportedly engraved, not embellished

indicators.note: reportedly means by word of mouth, so a word that is heard rather than seen is wanted

parts.note: metal that is chased has a pattern engraved on it

explanation.surface: A piece of silver said to be engraved turns out to be plain.
explanation.walkthrough: Chasing is decorating metal by engraving; the word is pronounced exactly like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaste style in design or writing is simple, restrained and free of ornament.

clue.text: Cover for locks in the rain, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words before it might be rearranged into something else

parts.note: the letters of both words, taken together

explanation.surface: Something to keep one's hair dry in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: Locks pretends, with cover, to be about doors; they are tresses of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine mesh worn over the hair holds it in place, so it covers someone's locks.

clue.text: Deputize for demonstration

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to take someone's place for a while, as a phrasal verb
second meaning: a protest where people occupy a place and refuse to leave

explanation.surface: Standing in for someone at a protest march.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means substitute for a colleague, and the hyphenated noun is an occupation-style protest.

clue.text: Testing points on saw

parts.note: two compass points, east and south
a saw is an old proverb

explanation.surface: Checking how sharp the teeth on a saw are.
explanation.walkthrough: Saw is the noun for a proverb, not the cutting tool or the past of see.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is to try or attempt it, so trying it out is testing it.

clue.text: Fail to observe as many as 5

definitions.note: 5 is the answer to 5 across, which means pure

parts.note: to spot something is to notice it
failing to see as many things as before is seeing fewer of them
surface padding that completes the phrase: failing to notice as many things

explanation.surface: Someone who misses as many details as the previous answer suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: Fail to observe as many reads as spot less: notice fewer things.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless and the answer to 5 across both describe someone pure and morally unblemished.

clue.text: Fit in girl's pockets

indicators.note: one word goes in the other, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a miss is a girl, and the apostrophe-s supplies the final letter
fit and suitable are synonyms

explanation.surface: A shapely figure in a young woman's coat pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: Pockets looks like part of a coat, but it is a verb: steals for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pockets money that is not theirs takes it dishonestly, which is embezzling.

clue.text: Cover, too, put round article

indicators.note: putting one thing round another means it surrounds it

parts.note: too much is overly
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A dust cover also placed round an item.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer laid on top of something else, such as a veneer, is a covering.

clue.text: Occupation for the heartless French city girl

indicators.note: a heartless word has had its middle letter taken out

parts.note: taken as written
Nancy is both a city in Lorraine and a girl's name

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted woman from France looking for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: Occupation looks like a job, but here it is the occupying of a property.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenancy is the holding or occupying of a house or land as a tenant, so occupation.

clue.text: Breakfast cooking done by prisoners

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the oat dish heated for the morning meal
second meaning: British slang for a jail sentence, which inmates are said to do

explanation.surface: Prison inmates on kitchen duty making the morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, doing porridge means serving time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The oatmeal dish is eaten in the morning, and in slang the word means time served inside.

clue.text: Light-hearted plot brought up during broadcast

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing something up means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: a bed is a plot in a garden
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A cheerful storyline mentioned in a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Plot suggests a storyline; it is a flower bed. During simply joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A debonair person is carefree and cheerfully self-assured, which is a light-hearted manner.

clue.text: The old city in Cannes, some say? No, in Italy

definitions.note: a city found in Italy, set against Cannes in France

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other
what some people say is spoken, so the place name is heard as a similar-sounding word

parts.note: Cannes is pronounced like cans, and a can is a tin
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in crosswords

explanation.surface: A tourist asks whether an old city is near Cannes and is told it is in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The French resort is a red herring; only its sound matters. Ur is the city of Abraham.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in Piedmont, north-west Italy, so it lies in that country.

clue.text: Made good company, highly respected outside

indicators.note: something placed outside surrounds the other piece

parts.note: revered means deeply respected
CO is the standard abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A firm that succeeded and is now held in high esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: Made good suggests success; here it means recouped, as in recovering a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: To make good a loss is to get it back, so what was regained has been retrieved.

clue.text: Deduce opposing argument's correct

parts.note: the cons are the arguments against, as in pros and cons
the apostrophe-s is read as is
correct and true are synonyms

explanation.surface: Concluding that the other side in a debate has a point.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe words is to interpret them and infer their meaning, so it is to work out or infer.

clue.text: Final character puts back a stone on ring

indicators.note: putting the whole sequence back means reading it in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
a precious stone is a gem
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A jeweller's last customer returns a ring with a stone set on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Final character is not a person; it is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is the closing letter.

clue.text: Kindly has object raised in well

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: doing something well is doing it ably

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word means reading it upwards

parts.note: your object is your aim or goal

explanation.surface: A kind person has hauled up something dropped down a well.
explanation.walkthrough: Well looks like a water source; it is the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a friendly, good-natured and pleasant way is acting kindly.

clue.text: Kind of herring found in the Archipelago

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pickled herring fillet named after the German chancellor

definitions.note: the clue means the name found in that archipelago's title
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the island group off New Guinea named after the same statesman

explanation.surface: A type of fish caught among a group of islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the pickled fish and the Pacific island group near Papua New Guinea carry the name of Germany's Iron Chancellor.

clue.text: Meet a supporter? Great

definitions.note: meet as an old adjective meaning fitting

parts.note: taken as written
a prop is something that supports
OS is the abbreviation for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: An invitation to meet a fan, greeted with enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: Meet is not the verb but the archaic adjective, as in 'it is meet and right'.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means appropriate or to the point, matching the old sense of suitable or proper.

clue.text: Collect, for instance, a mantis

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short ... read in church services on a set day
second meaning: one who prays, as the praying mantis seems to with its folded forelegs

explanation.surface: A collector gathers insects, a mantis for example.
explanation.walkthrough: Collect is the noun stressed on the first syllable, a liturgical item, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A collect is a short church petition to God, and the insect is named for its praying posture.

clue.text: Quiet like Peacock, say, or like another author

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
a peacock is an example of a bird, so like one is birdlike; the first 'like' does that work

explanation.surface: Comparing a reserved writer to the novelist Thomas Love Peacock.
explanation.walkthrough: Peacock is also a novelist, hence another author; the answer relates to George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Shavian describes the style, wit or ideas of the playwright George Bernard Shaw.

clue.text: School not keeping ahead enough?

indicators.note: not keeping the front part means the opening letters are dropped

parts.note: a school of thought sets a model to be followed

explanation.surface: A pupil falls behind and wonders whether they have done enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, more than sufficient for what is needed.

clue.text: Old money, including sovereign, for competitor

indicators.note: including something means taking it inside

parts.note: a stiver was a small old Dutch coin
R stands for rex or regina, a monarch

explanation.surface: Antique coins, among them a gold sovereign, offered as a prize for a contestant.
explanation.walkthrough: Sovereign suggests the old gold coin alongside old money; it is the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who strives makes great efforts to win, so is a contender in a contest.

clue.text: Part of flight in fastest airliner

indicators.note: the answer is sitting inside the words that follow

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A leg of a journey on the speediest passenger jet.
explanation.walkthrough: Flight looks like an air journey; it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps is made of single steps, each one a part of the whole.

clue.text: Antidemocratic organization?

parts.note: surface reading: a body hostile to democracy, such as a dictatorship
setter's reading: opposed to the Democrats, the rival US political party

explanation.walkthrough: The capital-free word democratic hides the American party; its rival is opposed to Democrats, not to democracy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand Old Party in the United States stands against the Democrats in elections.

clue.text: Diarist's boy or girl

definitions.meaning: first meaning: John ..., seventeenth-century English diarist
second meaning: a first name given to both males and females

explanation.surface: Someone keeping a diary writes about a child.
explanation.walkthrough: John Evelyn kept a diary alongside Samuel Pepys; Evelyn Waugh is a famous man with the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn was a famous seventeenth-century journal writer, and the first name is used for males and females alike.

clue.text: Campaigner's more blunt about South Africa

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a cruder remark is a blunter one
SA is the abbreviation for South Africa

explanation.surface: An activist speaks more bluntly about South Africa, apartheid then being a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader fights energetically for a cause, which is what a campaigner does.
